Number of threads used by HeatmapR

Source: R/heat_map_threads.R
heat_map_threads.Rd

The compiled code shares its larger jobs between threads: the distances between rows, the searches for the nearest cluster and the distance updates of the linkage while many clusters remain (more than about 1,500), the groups and the nearest-medoid search of two-stage clustering, the resamples of branch support (tree_support_x, tree_support_y) and the larger steps and blocks of optimal leaf ordering. Results are the same whatever the number of threads.

Usage

heat_map_threads(threads = NULL)

Arguments

threads

the number of threads to use from now on (a whole number of at least 1), NULL to leave it as it is, or NA to return to the default.

Value

the number of threads in use. When threads is given, the number in use before, invisibly.

Details

By default HeatmapR uses one thread per physical core, but no more than the CPUs the R process may run on (on Linux, e.g. when limited by taskset or a container), no more than the environment variables OMP_THREAD_LIMIT and OMP_NUM_THREADS allow (when they are set) and no more than two while R CMD check limits the number of cores (_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_). Processes forked from R (e.g. by parallel::mclapply()) use one thread unless the number is set. The linkage stops sharing its scans between threads when waiting for them takes longer than the work they save, e.g. when other processes keep the cores busy; results are the same either way. Set the number with heat_map_threads(n) or options(HeatmapR.threads = n), e.g. heat_map_threads(1) when heatmaps are drawn in parallel processes.

Examples

# THREADS IN USE
heat_map_threads()
#> [1] 4

# ONE THREAD, THEN BACK TO THE PREVIOUS SETTING
old <- heat_map_threads(1)
heat_map_threads(old)
